segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics digest from September 28th, 2026.
Today we cover amazing advancements, including breakthroughs in aquatic robotics, new advancements in AI programming, and exciting developments in autonomous systems.
From Robohub, "Small, medium or large, a robotic fish maintains its swimming ability".
This story details the development of a robotic fish model capable of maintaining swimming ability across different sizes.

Engineers at EPFL and NYU developed ScaFi, a robot modeled after a fish, utilizing a flexible tail constructed with proportional fiberglass rods that adjust in diameter to replicate the fish-like bending motion.
Testing with robots of varying lengths confirmed that this fish-like swimming gait was successfully preserved across different scales.
However, the study indicated that while the swimming motion scaled effectively, maintaining proportional energy efficiency presented a more significant challenge.
This approach establishes a scalable platform for investigating swimming performance across diverse environmental niches.
The findings suggest a method for scaling biomimicry in robotic systems for broader performance analysis.
And that's all the circuits for today, September 28th, 2026!
Keep exploring the fascinating waters of robotics, and I'll catch you in the next broadcast.
